I see a lot of apprehension about Tor and the "dark web" in this thread. To be sure, yes, there is illegal stuff on the tor network. What stuff is illegal depends on the country you are in and in some places tor use is illegal or strongly discouraged. Those are usually considered oppressive governments.

But there is nothing inherently wrong about using tor and browsing the deep web. Sure you may come across things that are morally abhorrent but those are pretty easy to steer clear of. Mostly, it's full of markets, conspiracy theories, hacking news, porn and websites that don't work.

The other thing that is handy is that tor obfuscates your traffic to your local network and your ISP. An it conceals your location from websites you visit. They'll know you are accessing tor or that your traffic is coming from a tor node but in general they can't tell much else. It makes it more difficult for corporations to track your browsing habits.

Government surveillance is another thing. Sure they can probably do a lot to track you through tor but not every is owned by them. Also, do you know a quicker and easier way for a non technical person living in an oppressive country to be able to access news and social media? I can't think of one.
